purpose: library: the carbon cycle under fossil-fuel forcing, with the modern CO2 record — continuous Mauna Loa observations since 1958 (global CO2 already 315 ppm then); 2024 global average 422.8 ppm; the growth rate about 0.8 ppm per year in the 1960s, doubling to 1.6 ppm per year in the 1980s; El Niño years tending to bring the largest annual increases; natural sinks (plant growth, ocean absorption) absorbing only part of emissions while fossil fuels overwhelm the natural carbon cycle; ice-core evidence that over the past 800,000 years CO2 never exceeded 300 ppm and was 280 ppm or less before the Industrial Revolution; the recent rise being about 100 times faster than previous natural increases; and scenario futures (emissions possibly reaching 75 billion tons per year). Fits quiz cards with predict-then-reveal on the ppm and growth-rate figures, a compare table of ice-age vs pre-industrial vs 2024 concentrations, and step ordering of the emissions→sink→concentration chain; the page's time-series records are charts as images.
